_comment: Issue #1370. Registers the snapshot-staleness detector inside check-skill-coverage-map.py's axis 2 (dependency): the sub-check that must notice when the vendored skillc profile-diagnose snapshot no longer matches the CURRENT codex/skills/<skill>/ closure, and therefore refuse to silently reuse a cached 'intact'/'broken' verdict. It does not cover axis 1 (content digest comparison), which is plain SHA-256 over text this script reads directly and needs no control of its own under the ADR 0008 bound - nothing about it is vendored or stale-prone.
detect_signal: ^skill-coverage-map: \S+ \([^)]+\): unknown - vendored diagnose\(\) snapshot is stale
limits: Covers only the closure-digest drift check that gates axis 2's read of the vendored diagnose() result - the one sub-behavior cpp-orch asked be proven able to fail the other way if disabled (#1370). Both cases hold axis 1 CURRENT (the fixture SKILL.md's description/body digests match the snapshot's reference exactly) so axis 1's short-circuit (check_skill returns at 'stale (content)' before axis 2 ever runs) cannot mask what this control is isolating. Fixtures are CONSTRUCTED, not vendored from a real skillc run: the reference digests, closure digests and diagnose() result are all synthetic JSON built to the schema check-skill-coverage-map.py reads, not output copied from an actual skillc invocation - skillc cannot run in CI and this control must. Declared gap: this control does not exercise a missing snapshot, a missing reference section, an absent skill directory, or axis 2's 'broken' status path (stale (dependency)) - those are pinned by tests/test_skill_coverage_map.py instead, which the ADR 0008 bound does not require a registered control for (a unit test the surrounding suite would catch).

anchors.why: CONSTRUCTED rather than historical: this gate is new in the same change that registers this control, so no pre-fix commit exists to vendor. The anchor is the real gate with exactly one edit - the line computing `drift` from `_diff_digests(snapshot_digests, current_digests)` replaced with a hardcoded empty list - reproducing the exact failure mode a reviewer found and fixed by hand during this change: disable the comparison and axis 2 falls straight through to reading the vendored diagnose() result's cached status as if it still described the current closure. On bad-snapshot-drift-not-detected (a closure that grew a file after the snapshot was recorded, with axis 1 held current) the anchor reports `current`/exit 0 instead of `unknown`/exit 1 - it silently reuses the stale snapshot. On good-current it agrees with the real gate (`current`/exit 0), so the miss is isolated to the disabled comparison and not a generally broken gate.
